nodes.rationale: A decompiler or config change is inert until task extract is re-run, because the game loads baked .fr3 and .go files produced offline.

nodes.label: Texture extraction and baking workflow
nodes.rationale: Textures are not loaded as loose PNGs at runtime; they are baked into binary texture pages and .fr3 files during offline task extract.

nodes.label: Texture replacement directory structure (texture_replacements, _all, texture_merges)
nodes.rationale: Over a third of retail textures are shared across levels, so _all/ is the global fallback when a texture is genuinely shared.

nodes.label: Merc .fr3 injection (no-borrow workflow)
nodes.rationale: Declaring extra_art_groups_by_dgo with an art-group:HOME.DGO pairing bakes a model's geometry into another level without burning scarce level-borrow slots; omitting the home DGO may pick a level lacking the right texture page.

nodes.label: Non-destructive texture and UV management
nodes.rationale: Never modify decompiled archives or retail textures; place PNGs under custom_assets texture_replacements and bake with task extract.

nodes.label: Texture reachability: two disjoint pipelines
nodes.rationale: Classic texture-page lookup (hud-sprite, def-tex) and the PC-port TexturePool read by Merc2 are separate; a custom-baked texture never emits a real texture-page upload so it never crosses the narrow VIF-packet bridge. Draw custom textures on HUD as a spawned merc model, or repaint existing retail textures via texture_replacements.

nodes.label: 2-circuit architecture for skeletal actors
nodes.rationale: Circuit 1 (GOAL heap, art-group .go) makes an actor logically exist; Circuit 2 (PC Merc2 renderer, geometry baked into level .fr3 by task extract) makes it visible. A missing Circuit 2 bake gives a silently invisible model; a missing Circuit 1 load crashes with process-drawable-art-error.

nodes.label: Double-Buffered GS Output with XGKICK
nodes.rationale: Two GS vertex buffers (offsets 0 and 176) alternate per sprite so the next sprite can be built while the previous one is kicked to the GS.

nodes.label: Pie-Slice Circle Vertex Construction
nodes.rationale: A distort sprite is a circle built from N pie-slices; each loop iteration emits 5 GS vertices for one slice.

nodes.label: ExecutionContext and fake stack (mips2c_call_systemv)
nodes.rationale: Saving all registers costs 1-2 kB of stack, so suspends inside mips2c code will probably fail; a cleverer scheme was judged not worth it.

nodes.label: gMips2CLinkCallbacks and link() mechanism
nodes.rationale: Symbol lookups are cached in a Cache structure instead of patching code; the linker calls the registered link() when the matching object file is linked.

nodes.label: Mips2C converter
nodes.rationale: Literal op-by-op MIPS to C translation; with compiler optimizations it can beat OpenGOAL output and mostly just works for branch-heavy, 128-bit-GPR-dependent, not-understood or CFG-failing functions.
